name: Tribute
overview: Scripture teaches that tribute, often in the form of a fixed offering, was instituted as a means of atonement and service to the LORD, as seen in the command for every Israelite over twenty to give a half shekel as a ransom for their soul (Exodus 30:12-16). This requirement was equitable, with neither the rich nor the poor giving more or less than the prescribed amount, emphasizing a just and orderly system of contribution. Additionally, leaders were cautioned against accumulating excessive silver and gold for themselves (Deuteronomy 17:17), underscoring the principle that tribute should serve God's purposes rather than personal gain.
